bug_description.original: Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5725303486414848 Project: libsrtp Fuzzing Engine: honggfuzz Fuzz Target: srtp-fuzzer Job Type: honggfuzz_asan_libsrtp Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ {*} Crash Address: 0x602000000180 Crash State: srtp_stream_init_keys srtp_stream_init srtp_add_stream Sanitizer: address (ASAN) Recommended Security Severity: Medium Regressed: https://oss-fuzz.com/revisions?job=honggfuzz_asan_libsrtp&range=202109090600:202109100611 Reproducer Testcase: https://oss-fuzz.com/download?testcase_id=5725303486414848
bug_description.normalized: The staged 85-byte witness lets `extract_policy()` copy a first 32-byte policy record from the input. Its selector byte `0xf1` is reduced modulo the `fuzz_srtp_crypto_policies` table length, and both the 9-entry and 18-entry variants yield index `7`, selecting `srtp_crypto_policy_set_null_cipher_hmac_null` for both RTP and RTCP. That helper sets `cipher_type = SRTP_NULL_CIPHER` but incorrectly records `cipher_key_len = 16` instead of the 30-byte key-plus-salt length that `full_key_length(SRTP_NULL_CIPHER)` later expects. Because the same first record carries even `do_extract_key`, `extract_key()` allocates only a 16-byte `policy->key` buffer and copies 16 input bytes into it. The harness only reaches `srtp_create()` after a second `extract_policies()` call returns non-NULL; the saved witness leaves a trailing second 32-byte policy record for that gate. When `srtp_add_stream()` processes the first policy, it validates only key presence and MKI bounds, not the required key length for the chosen cipher. `srtp_stream_alloc()` then allocates null-cipher session objects for RTP and RTCP, so `session_keys->rtp_cipher->type` and `session_keys->rtcp_cipher->type` both resolve to `SRTP_NULL_CIPHER`. `srtp_stream_init_all_master_keys()` aliases the 16-byte heap buffer into `master_key->key`, `srtp_stream_init_keys()` computes `input_keylen = full_key_length(SRTP_NULL_CIPHER) = 30`, and `memcpy(tmp_key, key, input_keylen)` over-reads 30 bytes from the 16-byte allocation. The fix corrects both null-cipher policy helpers to use `SRTP_AES_ICM_128_KEY_LEN_WSALT` instead of `16`.

evidence_note: This pass rebuilt the GT after applying the concrete issues recorded in `trace_feedback.json`. `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so no instrumentation was added. The selector proof stays source-grounded without any build-mode assumption because `0xf1 % 9 = 7` and `0xf1 % 18 = 7`, so the first policy selects `srtp_crypto_policy_set_null_cipher_hmac_null` whether or not the optional OpenSSL-only table entries are compiled in.
evidence_limitations: Stage 02 rebuilt the trace from the saved vulnerable source tree, patch, PoC bytes, compile/run logs, sanitizer trace, and reviewer feedback; it did not rerun the PoC or dynamically validate the fixed build.

Because `runtime_disambiguation` is disabled in `run_flags.json`, no extra instrumentation was added; the trace stays source-grounded and uses the saved crash only as runtime evidence that the documented path was actually reached.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that copies attacker-controlled bytes into the policy-parameter struct later used to select the vulnerable null-cipher helper and the direct-key extraction path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is an 85-byte raw testcase. After `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` consumes the first 4 bytes as little-endian `randseed = 0x20202020`, this statement copies the first 32-byte policy record into `params`. In the staged witness, that record begins with selector byte `0xf1`, carries `num_xtn_hdr = 0`, `do_extract_key = 0x20`, and `do_extract_master_keys = 0x20`, and the next 16 bytes at offsets 36..51 are all `0x20` and later become the undersized heap key buffer.

root_cause.description: The null-cipher policy helper stores a 16-byte key length even though null-cipher SRTP still expects the AES-ICM key-plus-salt length. This incorrect policy state is later trusted by the fuzzer's key extraction logic.
root_cause.note: The selected helper runs for both `policy->rtp` and `policy->rtcp`. The staged patch changes this exact field from `16` to `SRTP_AES_ICM_128_KEY_LEN_WSALT`, i.e. 30 bytes.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `srtp_stream_init_keys()` copies `input_keylen` bytes from the caller-supplied master-key buffer into a large local `tmp_key` array; with the staged witness, `input_keylen` is 30 while `key` points to a 16-byte heap allocation.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 30` at `srtp/srtp.c:965:5`, and its allocation stack identifies the 16-byte source region allocated in `extract_key()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This call materializes the over-read source buffer. The caller supplies `key_size = 16`, so `extract_key()` allocates a 16-byte heap region and copies exactly 16 attacker-controlled bytes into it.
tainted_value_origin.note: ASan's allocation stack points at this exact allocation path: `fuzz_alloc -> fuzz_alloc_succeed -> extract_key -> extract_policy`.

parser_admitted.description: The first policy record is present in the staged witness, so `extract_policy()` does not take its early `goto end;` path and commits to building a live `srtp_policy_t` from attacker-controlled bytes.
parser_admitted.note: Bytes 4..35 are present, so the first root-cause policy is materialized instead of taking the parser's early `goto end` path.

second_policy_chain_present.description: The harness only calls `srtp_create()` after a second `extract_policies()` call succeeds, so the witness must also preserve a second non-NULL policy chain after the first root-cause policy has been parsed.
second_policy_chain_present.note: After the first chain consumes the 32-byte params record and the 16-byte direct key, byte 52 ends that chain. The saved crash stack reaches `srtp_create()` and `srtp_add_stream()`, and source-wise bytes 53..84 provide the second call's required 32-byte `params` record at `extract_policy()`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness consumes a 4-byte randseed, parses a first policy whose selector and direct-key bytes drive the bug, and requires a trailing second policy record so the `policy_chain_2` gate passes before `srtp_create()`.
Policy extraction reduces selector byte `0xf1` to index `7`, selects `srtp_crypto_policy_set_null_cipher_hmac_null` for RTP and RTCP, and extracts only a 16-byte heap key buffer.
libsrtp accepts the malformed null-cipher policy, allocates session cipher objects from its null-cipher type, and carries the same 16-byte `policy->key` into stream-key initialization.
Key initialization derives a required length of 30 bytes from `SRTP_NULL_CIPHER` and `memcpy`s 30 bytes from the 16-byte heap key, triggering the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: Copies the first policy record from the attacker-controlled byte stream into `params`, making the policy selector, `do_extract_key`, and the later key bytes live parser state.

This normalization maps selector byte `0xf1` to index `7` whether `fuzz_srtp_crypto_policies` has 9 entries or 18, so the first policy selects `fuzz_srtp_crypto_policies[7]`, `srtp_crypto_policy_set_null_cipher_hmac_null`.

The selected helper writes inconsistent policy state: both RTP and RTCP become `SRTP_NULL_CIPHER`, but their required application-supplied key length is recorded as only 16 bytes instead of the 30-byte key-plus-salt length later expected by libsrtp.
Witness byte `0x20` is even, so the first policy takes the direct-key path and will populate `policy->key` instead of leaving it `NULL`.

Called from step 4 with `key_size = policy->rtp.cipher_key_len = 16`, `extract_key()` allocates a 16-byte heap buffer and copies the next 16 witness bytes into it. This is the exact 16-byte region later named by ASan as the over-read source.

The malformed null-cipher policy is accepted here. `srtp_valid_policy()` only rejects `deprecated_ekt`, and `srtp_validate_policy_master_keys()` checks only that a key pointer exists and MKI sizes are bounded. No guard compares the supplied 16-byte key buffer against the 30-byte length later required for `SRTP_NULL_CIPHER`.

fine_trace.code:
stat = srtp_crypto_kernel_alloc_cipher(
            p->rtp.cipher_type, &session_keys->rtp_cipher,
            p->rtp.cipher_key_len, p->rtp.auth_tag_len);
...
        stat = srtp_crypto_kernel_alloc_cipher(
            p->rtcp.cipher_type, &session_keys->rtcp_cipher,
            p->rtcp.cipher_key_len, p->rtcp.auth_tag_len);
fine_trace.note: Stream allocation materializes the policy's null-cipher choice into session state. For `SRTP_NULL_CIPHER`, the callee `srtp_null_cipher_alloc()` stores `(*c)->type = &srtp_null_cipher`, so both `session_keys->rtp_cipher->type` and `session_keys->rtcp_cipher->type` now identify the null cipher that step 9 queries.

Because step 5 produced a non-NULL `policy->key`, initialization takes the direct-key branch, aliases that same 16-byte heap buffer as `single_master_key.key`, and passes it into `srtp_stream_init_keys()` for the session state created in step 7.
Because the session-level cipher objects from step 7 both point at `srtp_null_cipher`, `full_key_length(...)` takes the `SRTP_NULL_CIPHER` case and derives `input_keylen = 30`.

The destination `tmp_key` is a 256-byte stack array, so the fault is entirely on the source side: this `memcpy` reads `input_keylen = 30` bytes from the 16-byte heap buffer aliased in step 8. ASan reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow read of size 30 at this exact statement.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch replaces `cipher_key_len = 16` in both null-cipher helper functions with `SRTP_AES_ICM_128_KEY_LEN_WSALT`, so the same witness drives `extract_key()` to allocate a 30-byte master-key buffer that matches `full_key_length(SRTP_NULL_CIPHER)`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context is the 16-byte fuzzer-side key buffer, while the earlier logical root cause is the null-cipher helper's incorrect `cipher_key_len = 16`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_38359 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` file to `/out/srtp-fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 30` in `srtp_stream_init_keys`.

format.contract: The staged witness is exactly the 85-byte `poc` file. Bytes 0..3 are the little-endian randseed `0x20202020`. Bytes 4..35 form the first policy record; selector byte `0xf1` reduces to index `7` for either the 9-entry or 18-entry `fuzz_srtp_crypto_policies` table, selecting `srtp_crypto_policy_set_null_cipher_hmac_null`. The same first record carries even `do_extract_key = 0x20`, so `extract_policy()` calls `extract_key()` with `key_size = 16`, and bytes 36..51 become the 16-byte `policy->key` buffer later over-read. The staged harness also requires a second non-NULL `policy_chain_2`: byte 52 stops additional policies in the first chain, and bytes 53..84 supply the second call's 32-byte `params` record before `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` reaches `srtp_create()`.
